newsitem.title: USA: Walgreen profits rise, charge cuts Rite Aid net.
newsitem.headline: Walgreen profits rise, charge cuts Rite Aid net.

text.p: Drugstore giant Walgreen Co. Monday posted record profits, while rival Rite Aid Corp. said its net earnings fell after a charge for its acquisition of Thrifty Payless Corp.
Walgreen said net earnings for the second quarter ended Feb. 28 rose 16 percent to a record $147 million, or 59 cents a share, from $126.8 million, or 51 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Sales grew 13 percent to $3.6 billion from $3.2 billion.
Chairman Charles Walgreen III said the strong results were aided by good expense controls, an excellent holiday selling season and strong pharmacy sales, which rose 17.5 percent for the quarter.
Pharmacy sales in stores open for at least a year rose 12.2 percent for the quarter. Total comparable store sales rose 8.0 percent for both the quarter and the six months.

"Our prescription business now accounts for more than 45 percent of our total sales," said Walgreen. "We project this business to get even stronger in the future as the baby boomers age and as more and more people find themselves in managed care."
Walgreen said it was on track to open 230 new stores during this fiscal year. As of Feb. 28, the Deerfield, Ill.-based company had 2,256 drugstores in 34 states and Puerto Rico vs. 2,131 a year ago.

Rite Aid, the nation's second-largest drugstore chain, said its net income plunged to $10 million, or 9 cents a share, in the fourth quarter ended March 31, from almost $60 million, or 68 cents a share. The drop in earnings came after an extraordinary, after-tax loss of $45.2 million, or 38 cents a share, to pay off Thrifty PayLess debt.

Rite Aid, based in Camp Hill, Pa., completed its $1.4 billion acquisition of Thrifty PayLess Holdings Inc. on Dec. 12. The merger created a chain of more than 3,500 drugstores with annual revenues of more than $10 billion.
The company said, however, that excluding one-time items operating income rose to $87.6 million, or 75 cents a share, from almost $57 million, or 68 cents a share, in the same period in 1995.
Rite Aid was knocked off the top of the list of the nation's largest drugstore chains after the $1.8 billion merger of CVS Corp. and Revco D.S. Inc. announced in February.
Rite Aid's sales for the 13-week quarter jumped 86 percent to $2.7 billion from $1.4 billion. Thrifty PayLess stores accounted for $1.2 billion of the revenue.
Total same-store sales for Rite Aid stores grew 10.1 percent and pharmacy same-store sales rose 14.4 percent.
Walgreen's stock fell $1.25 to $41.625, while Rite Aid rose 75 cents to $42.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
